explanations.text:
●  you open the feed                                            ([the page](html))
  │     You open /human/feed.html on the same address as the reader.
  │     The page is dark and fills the screen, one card at a time,
  │     the way a video feed does ([the look](style)). Its title
  │     says Human · feed ([the title](title)).
  │
  ●  the page finds the session                                      ([the load](load))
  │     It asks the tool for the list of sessions and takes the one
  │     you named in the address, else the newest one still open,
  │     else the newest of all ([the choice](wanted)). Then it asks
  │     for that session's file and draws it, and asks again every
  │     five seconds, so a row claude adds while you read appears
  │     on its own.
  │
  ●  the top bar says where you are                                ([the bar](renderTop))
  │     A list to switch sessions, OPEN or FINISHED, and the count:
  │     how many files, how many picked.
  │
  ●  each file is one row, each version one card                 ([the rows](renderRows))
  │     Swipe down for the next file. Swipe sideways for the next
  │     version of the same file — three cards in a strip
  │     ([the strip](rowHtml)). When the tool changes one row, only
  │     that row is redrawn ([one row](rerenderRow)), and it keeps
  │     the card you were on.
  │
  ●  a card shows one version                                       ([the card](cardHtml))
  │     At the top: the file, the kind of row, where the text will go,
  │     "carried" for a row from an earlier session, and the name of
  │     the version — "current" for the middle of a sync row while it
  │     still holds the map's own text. A "copy" button stands there
  │     when the slot has text. Under it the text, with every pinned
  │     word marked ([the marks](textHtml)); an empty slot says
  │     "not written yet".
  │
  ●  you pick, and say why if you want                              ([the script](script))
        One tap on "pick this one" opens a box for the reason; you may
        leave it empty. "pick" sends the row, the version and the
        reason to the tool ([the send](sendPick)); "cancel" closes the
        box. The answer is the row as the tool now keeps it: the
        picked card turns blue, the two others say which one you
        picked, and your reason stands under the text. A tap on the
        picked card takes the pick back.

──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  when the session is finished
     Every card says what happened to its row: the pick, the reason,
     and the entry the pick became. Nothing can be picked any more.

  when you take the text away                                    ([the copy](copyText))
     One tap on "copy" puts that version's text on the clipboard and
     the button says "copied" for a moment — also on a plain http
     address, where the browser's own clipboard door stays shut.

  when there is nothing to show                          ([the empty page](renderEmpty))
     No session yet, or the tool not reachable: one line in the
     middle of the screen says which.

  when you switch sessions
     The list in the top bar writes the session into the address,
     so a reload — or a link — opens the same one.

  a word of text stays a word                                     ([the escape](esc))
     Anything the text holds is shown as it is, never read as part
     of the page.
